resolvedIdentity: Kornsjø station, the historic protected border-station complex on the Østfold Line at Nordre Kornsjø.

coordinateDecision.reason: The legacy coordinate was more than 17 kilometres north of Kornsjø. The applied point is the named station entity and aligns with Bane NOR, heritage and specialist railway sources.

sources.name: Wikidata – Kornsjø station
findings: Bane NOR location code KO and linear position 169.12 km.

sources.name: Bane NOR – Kornsjø station
findings: Kornsjø station is on the Østfold Line, 169.12 km from Oslo S.
The official track table shows several main, passing and additional tracks.

sources.name: Jernbane.net – Kornsjø station
findings: The first wooden building followed Peter Andreas Blix type drawings.
It burned in 1898 and was replaced by a larger masonry station by Paul Due, completed in 1900.
The larger building also accommodated customs functions.
All passenger service ended in 1999 and the building was protected in 2001.

sources.name: Kornsjø local history – station
findings: The original 1879 timber station burned in August 1898.
The replacement station was completed in 1900 after greater customs-space requirements.

sources.name: Wikidata – Kornsjø border
findings: It lies approximately 950 metres south-east of Kornsjø station.

sources.name: Riksantikvaren – Kornsjø locomotive shed decision
usedFor: separate locomotive-shed condition and ownership context
findings: The locomotive shed is a separate technical-industrial heritage component near the station.
The document distinguishes it from the protected station building and records condition and access concerns.

dateHandling.dayDateDecision: Do not encode an exact opening day in canonical narrative because sources vary between 18 and 25 July 1879.

accessAndSafety: Passenger trains do not stop, but the railway infrastructure remains operational.
No task may require walking on or crossing tracks outside authorised public crossings.
Technical buildings and the protected station building may have separate ownership and access rules.
The 300-metre radius is not a track, railway, heritage, property, platform, customs or safety boundary.
